_: What to ASK the generator for. `generated.json` beside this holds the ids that came BACK and is what ships; this holds the words, so a body can be re-asked, re-rolled or asked for again on a fresh account without anybody reconstructing what was said. `tools/art/body.mts` reads it.
_say: A state's `say` is `action_description` and the tool warns off environment: movement and pose only, and no room, no floor, no light. Two things are learned and both are in here — naming a weapon the rotation does not hold invents a DIFFERENT one per frame, and an animation drifts off model across its run, so short is safer and 'side profile' is worth saying out loud.
_face: The ONE facing generated. It is an angled side profile — front on, but you can see which way a body faces — and the renderer mirrors it for the left half, so two directions cost one. Every quality failure the five-facing era had was a facing other than this one or a strict side.

A shaggy hide slung over ONE shoulder and belted at the waist, leaving the other shoulder and the whole chest bare and covered in dense black TATTOO work — solid blocks and sharp banded chevrons running up the neck and jaw, over the shoulder and down one whole arm to the knuckles. His skin is warm deep brown; his hide is dull rust, ochre and dark tan; the ink is near-black. BOTH HANDS EMPTY — no sword, no axe, no shield, no spear, no club, no weapon at all. He is a LIVING BREATHING MAN with FLESH on him, warm skin over most of him. Tall and long-limbed with a SMALL head. NOT a skull, NOT a skeleton, NOT undead, NOT armoured, NOT a breastplate, NOT chainmail, NOT a helmet, NOT a robe, NOT a mage, NOT a shirt, NOT a headdress, NOT feathers, NOT a mask, NOT face paint, NOT a bodybuilder, NOT oiled, NOT anime, NOT manga, NOT chibi, NOT cute, NOT a big head, NOT a doll, NOT a cartoon. FULL BODY head to feet, seen at a THREE-QUARTER angle, turned enough that you can tell which way he faces. No ground, no floor, no shadow cast on the ground, no base, no platform, no other objects.

idle.say: Standing still with his iron club, standing still, weight shifting from one foot to the other, chest rising and falling, arms loose at the sides. He keeps hold of it in EVERY frame and never lets go of it or puts it down. NOTHING else is in the picture: no second weapon, no shield, no other object, no glow, no magic, no sparks, no smoke, no aura, no dropped item, nothing floating beside him or at his feet. Only the man and what he is holding.

walk.say: Walking forward with his iron club, at a heavy unhurried pace, shoulders rolling, arms swinging from the shoulder. He keeps hold of it in EVERY frame and never lets go of it or puts it down.

attack.say: Attacking with his iron club, a two-beat CLUB SWING: he cocks the club back over his shoulder with the weight on the back foot, then swings it round and DOWN in front of him and steps through onto the front foot, ending with the club at full stretch low in front of him, seen at a three-quarter angle. He faces the same way in EVERY frame and never turns away from the viewer, and the animation ENDS at full extension with no recovery and no settling back. He keeps hold of it in EVERY frame and never lets go of it or puts it down.

cast.say: Casting with his iron club, strict side profile, planting both feet wide and hauling both fists in to the chest, then throwing the head back and roaring with the arms flung out, seen at a three-quarter angle. He keeps hold of it in EVERY frame and never lets go of it or puts it down.

death.say: Dying with his iron club, buckling at the knees, folding forward over the stomach and going down onto the side, lying flat and still, seen at a three-quarter angle. He keeps hold of it in EVERY frame and never lets go of it or puts it down.

_inks: A body is FORCED onto a palette by image, and the roster's own is dark bone and rust. A family living somewhere else needs its own: `inks` names one of these, and a body without the field takes the roster's. Eight dark swatches to four accents in each, because the forcing image is equal-area and the proportion is what lands.
_props: What a prop must SAY. `view` already defaults to high top-down and does not carry the framing on its own — the description has to, in capitals, or an object comes back 3/4-projected and reads as furniture from a different game. Naming a thing gets you ONE of it, so a scatter says 'spread apart with gaps'. And the palette words are the zone's own, by exclusion as well as by number, or a prop lands warmer and more cheerful than the stone around it. A `view` of `side` is for what hangs on the WALL FACE: the face is seen straight on, so a top-down picture of it lies flat against a cliff and reads as a sticker.

_design: A body is DESIGNED before it is rotated. `create_image_pixflux` draws one sprite from `look` for one generation; `create_character` in mode v3 with that PNG as `reference_image_base64` rotates it into eight directions for two more. `look` is the design ask and `states[].say` is the animation ask — and no two of a body's says may share their first 30 characters, because the server keys a type off that prefix and silently refuses the second.
_weapons: A row whose `sprite` is `<hero>_<weapon>` is a VARIANT: the same man drawn holding what he is carrying, so the arms are round it instead of a picture being pinned at his fist. Its `character` is a `create_character_state` of the hero's own, which keeps his identity and inherits his skeleton. The words for the weapon itself live in `weapons.json` and are shared by every hero — never write one into a body row.
